headline: FPGA-LDO A layout V12 (edited 10 Nov 2026, 16:06 CST) passes KiCad's checks (DRC, ERC and parity all 0), but it still follows pin map V5. It needs a pin map V6 revision (A-P on the ASIC list) before any order. The ASIC boards V4 close LDOA-04, because every chip now has its own SPI data lanes. This review adds 26 items, 8 of them major: Frontend capacitors over ±12 V copper, no panel method or tab positions set (V-cut is ruled out), switching noise that can upset CLK32 and the stimulation controls, controls that float when an ASIC joint is partly seated, and Option B repeating the ±10 V power-down fault. The 9 older majors are still open: the L11/L12 and U1 parts, ±10 V power-down, the LT3582 input capacitor, converter ripple and lane returns in AGND, and the thin J1/J2 ground. U1 is now in stock at DigiKey.
top_actions: Allocate pin map V6 together with the Frontend in one pass (A-P): 12 new lanes on J3/J4 pins 2/4/6/8/24/58, the 4 returned CLK32 lines moved to clock-capable balls, a 10k pull-down on J3.70 and J4.70 (LDOA-49 and LDOA-58 are one change), DRIVE/SLEW set in the new pin file (LDOA-62), and the PCB-5 notes rewritten (LDOA-17).

Send the ASIC designer one list of questions: input thresholds (LDOA-42), the VDD10/VSS10 maximum (LDOA-13), which ground each rail uses (LDOA-16), the REF_VCM load (LDOA-14) and the power-down order (LDOA-28).

Make one ground decision before re-routing: GND, not AGND, under the lane and CLK32 corridors (LDOA-02, LDOA-54); keep converter ripple off AGND and NT1, and put each regulator on the ground of the ASIC rail it feeds (LDOA-10, LDOA-11, LDOA-12, LDOA-16).

Settle the mating risks. Lower or remove Frontend C4/C42/C59, or clear the ±12 V copper under them (LDOA-37, with SYS-08/FE-04). Decide how the stimulation and reset inputs stay defined when a J3/J4 or near-to-far joint is partly seated: pulls on each ASIC board, or mating with power off plus a seating check (LDOA-43, LDOA-44, LDOA-56, LDOA-57).

Build V13 power first, then route the V6 lanes. Add vias in every J1/J2 GND pad (LDOA-05, LDOA-40); add a local LT3582 input capacitor and the Figure 12 grounding (LDOA-06, LDOA-51); add VDD10/VSS10 Schottky clamps (LDOA-08, LDOA-09; LDOA-39 if Option B stays); add more VIN and regulator ground vias (LDOA-18, LDOA-19, LDOA-52). Then simulate or measure CLK32 and STIM_START/EN while 10-14 outputs switch (LDOA-41, LDOA-42).

Close the order items. Secure U1 from DigiKey stock and add a '-12 only' note (LDOA-50, LDOA-07). Choose L11/L12 (LDOA-01). Decide D11/D12: the in-stock JSCJ B5819WS fits (LDOA-48). Reserve 20 TPS7A2015 (LDOA-32). Agree a panel with JLC (LDOA-38) and check the CPL rotations in JLC's preview (LDOA-24, LDOA-46).

findings.title: On Option A the only pulls on the ASIC control lines are on FPGA-LDO A, so a J3 or J4 joint lifted about 0.5-0.65 mm at its pin-80 end leaves four fully powered ASICs with both resets, IMP_TST, AC_IN and SPI_LATCH floating, and the stimulator controls float by about 0.73 mm, once four rails have opened.
findings.what: Every resistor that holds a stimulator or reset control in its safe state (R2-R6, R16-R19) is on FPGA-LDO A. The ASIC V4 boards have none, so the chips get those levels only through the J3/J4 contacts. All nine pulled controls sit on the odd contact row, on the side where the ASIC stack overhangs. All four grounds and eight of the nine rails sit on the even row. A joint that is not pushed fully home, or is rocked by a load, can therefore open the control row while the rail and ground row stays connected. The ASICs then stay powered with EN, START, CHB, STIM_CLK, both resets, the latch, IMP_TST and AC_IN connected to nothing. Nothing holds the stack: none of these boards has a hole, and the 80-position DF40C has no lock and no retention tab. The only drawing of the head puts FPGA-LDO A and the Frontend on J3/J4 above the ASIC boards, which rest on the skull. Frontend plugging and cable loads would then also pass through these joints.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO A V12 J3 (DF40C-80DP, top, centre 99.783/113.513; odd row y 112.158, even row y 114.868) and J4 (DF40C-80DS, bottom; odd 111.978, even 115.058). Odd row: STIM_CHB 49 (R4), STIM_EN 51 (R2), STIM_CLK 53 (R5), STIM_START 55 (R3), SPI_LATCH 61 (R18), FE_RESET 65 (R16), IMP_TST 67 (R17), AC_IN 69 (R6 to AGND), CHIP_RESET 71 (R19 to ASIC_DVDD); also VDD_CGEN 1, CLKH 7 and the unpulled per-chip SPI pins 23/25/57/59/63. Even row: DVDD 34 to VDD_ADC 56, AGND 42/44, GND 46/48. Chips: the J4 port carries ASIC1-4 and the J3 port ASIC5-8 (near chips 1/2 and 5/6, far chips 3/4 and 7/8).
findings.evidence: Pulls: W2/exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml; each control net is a J2 pin + J3 + J4 + its resistor. ASIC V4: W2/exports/asic_top/parts.csv and asic_bottom/parts.csv list 30 C, 3 J and 2 U with no resistor; board_stats shows NPTH 0 on all three boards. Contact model: a contact is open when its local withdrawal exceeds 0.45 mm (W2/a review working file (not published) and seat_windows_out.txt; J4 has the same pin x). (1) Lengthwise, pin-1 end seated (the critic's numbers confirmed): lifting the pin-80 end 0.50-0.65 mm floats CHIP_RESET, AC_IN, IMP_TST and FE_RESET (all four chips), SPI_LATCH and the near chips' SPI pins 57/59/63 (in pin map V6 also the far chips' latch, clock and data on 66-72), with all 9 rails and 4 grounds made. STIM_START/CLK/EN/CHB then open at 0.65-0.73 mm together with VDD_ADC/VSS10/REF_VDD/VDD_FE in the same columns. At 0.73-0.76 mm all nine float while DVDD, VDD10, VDD_DRIVER, REF_VCM, VDD_CGEN and all grounds stay made. (2) Across-row: with a uniform withdrawal w, all nine controls (plus VDD_CGEN and CLKH) open once the odd row rises an extra 0.45 - w mm, while the 8 even-row rails and 4 grounds stay made for any w below 0.45. At w = 0, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 mm this needs 8.3-9.4, 4.6-5.3, 2.8-3.2 and 0.9-1.1 degrees (3.08/2.71 mm row pitch). (3) Combined: if the pin-80 end is also at least 0.1 mm higher, an extra odd-row lift of 0.01-0.45 mm floats all nine with all 9 rails and 4 grounds made. Example: w 0.19 mm, pin-80 end +0.2 mm, odd row +0.2 mm (3.7-4.2 degrees), margins at least 0.06 mm (pose_check_out.txt). (4) Which row goes first (overhang_and_pose_out.txt): the V4 outline, turned 180 degrees about J3/J4 as in the V10 fit test, overhangs FPGA-LDO A's north edge by 10.29 mm. Its centroid is 4.95 mm past the connector centre line, 3.4-3.6 mm past the odd row. A load F pulling the stack away puts +1.9 to +2.3 F on the odd row and presses the even row (-0.9 to -1.3 F); a load pressing the stack on does the reverse. With the boards level: top port upright and bottom port inverted lose the even row first; top port inverted and bottom port hanging upright lose the odd row (controls) first. The deck's head view stands the stacks upright with the probe edge on the skull, so gravity acts in the board plane toward the overhang. That loses the even row first with the head upright and the odd row first with it inverted (about 1.0-1.4 F per row, with the centre of mass 3.0-3.9 mm from the joint). Two 1.6 mm boards weigh about 0.022 N (FR-4 at 1.9 g/cm3, from memory, not re-read). Gravity only decides which row a loose joint loses first; shocks and handling supply the force.

findings.consequence: With J3 or J4 partly out and the cable live, four ASICs can sit powered with floating stimulator, reset, latch and test inputs, and nothing on the head detects it. What the stimulator does then is not established (U05, U07). Unintended stimulation is possible but not shown, as is a phase left without charge balance because STIM_CLK stopped. In the first lengthwise window EN and START stay under FPGA control while the latch and the near chips' SPI lines float. A stray latch edge can then load undefined stimulus tables, which the next commanded stimulation runs.

findings.title: The far ASICs get their stimulator and reset controls through a second unretained DF40 joint, out of reach of any pull on or below the near board, so lifting one end of that joint 0.50-0.76 mm can float them while rails stay connected.
findings.what: On ASIC V4 the top (far) board's chips receive STIM_EN, STIM_START, STIM_CHB, STIM_CLK, FE_RESET, IMP_TEST, AC_IN and CHIP_RESET through the near board and then a second DF40 joint: the near board's J4 plug into the far board's J3 receptacle. That joint is as unretained as J3/J4 and has the same layout: these eight controls, CLKH and VDD_CGEN on the odd row, every other rail and all grounds on the even row. The pulls sit two joints away on FPGA-LDO A. A rocked or partly seated far board therefore floats these controls while the far chips stay powered, even with J3/J4 fully home. Unlike the near chips, the far chips' own SPI latch, clock and data sit on the even row. A rock toward the overhang leaves those connected while the stimulator controls float.

findings.title: LT3582 VIN pin 5 has no local input capacitor; it is fed through two microvias and 8.6 mm of 0.3 mm L5 trace.
findings.what: The LT3582 data sheet requires VIN to be bypassed locally with a ceramic capacitor, and its layout figure places the input capacitor right at pin 5. On V12, U1 pin 5 sits on a separate 2.36 mm2 L6 copper island holding only the pin and one microvia (a small laser-drilled via between adjacent layers); its only feed is 8.61 mm of 0.30 mm L5 trace to a second microvia under C1 (22 uF), 8.35 mm away. C11, the 4.7 uF part the schematic names as the converter's input capacitor, sits on the main VIN pour and reaches the pin only through the same trace. The inverting channel's pulsed switch current therefore flows in a loop (input capacitor, VIN, SWN, D12, C21, ground) about 8 x 4 mm instead of a few millimetres.
findings.evidence: pcbnew on a copy of the board (a review working file (not published), isl2.py; a review working file (not published)): the L6 /VIN_3V3 pour has two pieces, 113.21 mm2 and 2.36 mm2; the small piece holds only U1.5 and via (100.75, 144.85). L5 trace 1.414 + 7.2 = 8.61 mm at 0.30 mm; both vias drill 0.10 mm, pad 0.26 mm. Distances from U1.5 (exports/ldo_a/pads.csv): C1.1 8.35 mm, C11.1 4.43 mm, C2.1 9.71 mm. Loop bounding box about 8.2 x 4.0 mm. Schematic note: 'Changed from Figure 13: ... C1 -> C11 4.7 uF 10 V 0603'. Estimate: 0.3 mm trace between L4 GND (0.201 mm) and L6 (0.071 mm) is about 0.2-0.35 nH/mm, so 2-3 nH for the feed and 3-5 nH for the loop. At the 490-720 mA inverting current limit (p.3, reached at start-up) this gives a few tenths of a volt of spike at VIN; at the 10 mA design load peaks are much lower (p.10). No project record (V11_record, V12_record, V12_checks, parts_review_V21) lists this.

findings.suggested_action: Move C11 (or add a 1-4.7 uF ceramic plus 100 nF) directly at U1 pin 5 on the island, with a short ground via, and check the placement against data sheet Figure 12.

findings.title: ASIC_VDD10 has no clamp diode to AGND, so a power-down can pull the LT3042 output below its -0.3 V limit.
findings.what: The ASIC's stimulator sits between ASIC_VDD10 (+10 V from U9, an LT3042) and ASIC_VSS10 (-10 V from U10, an LT3094). After power is lost, ASIC current flowing only between the two rails drags them toward each other, while other paths drain each rail to ground at different rates, so one rail can cross 0 V. Where the rails end depends on the ASIC's current split and the regulators' shutdown currents, none of which is documented; in about two thirds of the modelled cases VDD10 goes below -0.3 V, the LT3042's absolute maximum, and an internal substrate diode (an unintended junction inside the chip) carries the current. In the other cases VSS10 ends up to about 2.5 V above AGND, which the LT3094 tolerates but for which the ASIC has no recorded tolerance.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12: U9 LT3042 OUT/OUTS pins 10/9 on ASIC_VDD10 with C902 (22 uF 1206, bottom, 94.925, 122.95); U10 LT3094 OUT/OUTS pins 10-12 on ASIC_VSS10 with C1002 (22 uF 1206, 106.75, 122.95) and C1004 (10 uF 0805, 103.45, 122.85); J3/J4 pin 36 (VDD10) and pin 54 (VSS10) to the ASIC boards.
findings.evidence: exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: ASIC_VDD10 = C902.1, J3.36, J4.36, U9.9, U9.10; ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J3.54, J4.54, U10.10-12; no diode, resistor or test point to AGND on either. D11/D12 are LT3582 converter diodes, not rail clamps. With only a load between the rails, the end voltage is 10 V x (Cp - Cn)/(Cp + Cn): -1.85 V with nominal 22/32 uF, about -1.6 V with typical derating. Ground-referenced drains shift this: LT3042 overshoot-recovery sink up to 15 mA (LT3042 p.21), LT3094 ground current, and the LT3582-12 VOUTN power-down discharge of 1.4/2.8/4.2 mA (3582512fb p.3), reaching VSS10 through the LT3094 OUT-to-IN diode. A sensitivity model with these drains (a review working file (not published); Cp 12-22 uF, Cn 30-64 uF, bridge current 0.1-8 mA, ground sinks 0-15 mA) has VDD10 crossing -0.3 V in about two thirds of cases and VSS10 ending +0.07 to +2.5 V in the rest. inputs/asic/J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv gives VDD10/VSS10 a 2 mA maximum each per ASIC board, so the original 23 mA load case is above budget. The ASIC boards add C18/C19 and C25/C26 (0201, no value given).

Neither data sheet shows a split-supply clamp; the need follows from the LT3042 rating. Read from local copies; analog.com timed out.
findings.consequence: On some power-downs the LT3042 output pin goes past its absolute maximum and its substrate diode carries a few mA; damage is unlikely but outside the data sheet. Where VSS10 ends positive instead, the ASIC's negative stimulator rail sits above AGND with no recorded tolerance.
findings.suggested_action: Add a Schottky from AGND (anode) to ASIC_VDD10 (cathode) beside C902, and optionally one from ASIC_VSS10 (anode) to AGND (cathode) beside C1002, rated VR of at least 20 V with VF under 0.3 V at 10-25 mA. Confirm with a scope on the first board, powering down with and without ASIC boards.

findings.title: On a light-load power-down, U10 (LT3094) output falls over 0.3 V below its input, past its absolute maximum.
findings.what: The LT3094 must never have OUT, OUTS or SET more than 0.3 V below IN, even in a fault. When 3.3 V is lost the LT3582 stops, but C3 holds EN_ASIC_RAILS up, so U10 stays on for about 49 ms (about 30-35 ms if C3 loses capacitance at 3.3 V bias). U10's own 2-4 mA ground current flows into its input node and raises it toward 0 V, while ASIC_VSS10 moves only with the ASIC load; with little or no load, including no ASIC boards fitted, the input passes the output and an internal substrate diode conducts. Pulling EN_ASIC_RAILS low with 3.3 V present (TP4 today) does the same for about 200 ms, because the LT3582-12 power-down discharge pulls U10's input toward ground while U10 is off.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12: U10 LT3094 (IN pins 1, 2, 13 and PGFB pin 5 on STIM_PRE_NEG; OUT pins 11/12 and OUTS pin 10 on ASIC_VSS10; SET pin 8 with C1003 1 uF and R1001 100k); input C1001 (10 uF, 107.725, 129.71) plus C21 (22 uF) through bridged JP2; output C1002 (22 uF) and C1004 (10 uF); EN_ASIC_RAILS (R1 10k, C3 4.7 uF, TP4, U1 pin 8 SHDN, U10 pin 3).
findings.evidence: exports/ldo_a/nets.csv: STIM_PRE_NEG = C1001.1, JP2.2, TP9.1, U10.1/2/5/13; STIM_NEG_12V = C21.1, D12.2, JP2.1, TP3.1, U1.2; ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J3.54, J4.54, U10.10-12. JP2 is 'Bridged' with real copper in the .kicad_pcb, so input and output are both 32 uF nominal; no diode or bleeder joins the two nets. Enable hold: R1 10k with the LT3582's 222k SHDN pull-down and C3 4.7 uF gives 45 ms x ln(3.16/1.06) = 49 ms nominal. To keep OUT above IN the ASIC must draw more than I_GND x Cout/Cin, about 2.4-4 mA at nominal capacitance and more with derating. Models (original shutdown2.py; a review working file (not published); a hand calculation): at 0-0.5 mA load OUT goes more than 0.5 V below IN in every case, starting about 6-34 ms after power loss, lasting about 15-40 ms, with about 0.5-2.6 mA in the diode; at 2 mA load in 4 of 6 cases. findings.title: The L2 AGND plane is the return plane for many L1 digital lanes, so their edge currents flow in analog ground.
findings.what: L2 is filled as the analog ground (AGND) plane and lies only 0.071 mm under L1, so for 216 of the 506 mm of L1 FPGA-to-ASIC lanes it carries their return current (the current that flows back under a signal trace in the nearest plane). These lanes are 1.5 V logic referenced to digital ground (GND), and AGND meets GND only at net tie NT1 (a deliberate copper join between two ground nets), so the return current must cross through NT1 or the small L2-L3 plane capacitance. The grounds of the LT3042 regulators that make REF_VCM, VDD_FE and REF_VDD land in the same plane, and 84 mm of the over-AGND lane length runs just north of them. The rest of the L1 lanes cross L2 voids and reference L3 GND, so they also change reference plane along their length.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO A V12, L1 lanes over the L2 (In1.Cu) AGND fill. Band y 128.6-133.8 just north of bottom-side U8 (93.2, 135.6, REF_VCM), U2 (98.85, 135.6, VDD_FE) and U6 (104.5, 135.6, REF_VDD). findings.title: The 14 Frontend GND pins on J1/J2 reach the ground planes only through thin L1 traces and three laser vias.
findings.what: J1 and J2 each have 7 GND pins spread over y 122.6-133.0. On this board each connector's GND pins are joined only by a 0.2 mm, 10.4 mm L1 trace, which drops to the L3/L4 GND planes through a 0.10 mm laser via (a small via through one thin layer) and a buried via: one such pair for J2, two for J1. These few vias carry the return current of about 108 signals on J1/J2 and the supply return of VIN_3V3 on J2.68-70. The trace adds roughly 2.5-7 nH of return inductance shared by up to 7 pins, which gives away most of the benefit of having 7 ground pins.

The original report counted the chain as one 54-square trace; each side actually has two parallel 0.2 mm traces, so the chain is about 28-29 squares (14-16 mOhm) and the voltage is about a quarter lower than first stated. findings.title: U3, U4 and U5 regulate against a different ground point from the ASIC's, so NT1 ripple lands on three rails.
findings.what: A regulator holds its output steady relative to its own ground pin, so if the load is decoupled to a different ground, any voltage between the two grounds appears on the rail at the load. U3 (VDD_ADC) is on GND, but the ASIC board decouples VDD_ADC to AGND; U5 (DVDD) is on AGND, but the ASIC board decouples DVDD to DGND; U4 (VDD_DRIVER) and its capacitors sit on an L6 AGND island that reaches the L2 plane only through NT1.2, about halfway along the NT1 tie. The NT1 ripple from the LT3582 therefore appears on these rails at the ASIC, hundreds of times above the ripple the TPS7A20 regulators pass from VIN_3V3. findings.what: This is the Option A version of LDOB-09, and it is larger. Data are launched on the CLK32 edge, so ground bounce from the switching outputs lands on that edge. Option A's clocks cross two joints. J3/J4 has 2 DGND and 2 AGND contacts for 44 outputs per port, and J1/J2 has the trunk of finding 1. Crosstalk alone keeps every edge monotonic. With 10-14 outputs switching one way, the model puts a step inside 0.525-0.975 V that the FPGA can cross twice. Under the V4 pin map the spare pins 2/4/6/8/24/58 carry far-chip outputs, so R2S-05's 'make the spares ground' fix is no longer available.

Crosstalk adds to it from STIM_CLK, and on STIM_EN also from ASIC1_SYNC, whose near-end crosstalk lands at the ASIC end. The ASIC's input thresholds and START's edge or level behaviour are unknown, so the margin cannot be proven either way.

findings.corrected: As drawn, ground bounce can put glitches of roughly 0.4-1.1 V on the idle-low shared STIM_START and STIM_EN inputs at the die pads when 10-14 ASIC outputs switch, assuming 25 ohm / 1 ns ASIC drivers. The glitch is about 0.2-0.65 V with 50 ohm drivers or 2 ns edges, and about 0.2-0.55 V once LDOA-05's pad vias are fitted. File this as a change to LDOA-05: fit its J1/J2 pad vias and ask the ASIC designer for VIH, hysteresis and how START is triggered. Do not add the proposed RC on the FPGA-LDO side of J3/J4: it does not remove the bounce at the two joints and can increase it, so any filtering must sit at the ASIC input.

findings.title: On FPGA-LDO A V12, Frontend C4, C42 and C59 sit over masked ±12 V stimulation copper, so if a worst-case contact wears through the mask, C4 could push +12 V into the FPGA core (1.1 V absolute maximum), while C42 and C59 would mainly short the -12 V supply.
findings.area: Stack clearance / copper under mated parts
findings.what: SYS-08 found that Frontend capacitors C4, C42 and C59 can be 1.45 mm tall in the 1.5 mm gap above this board, and noted only tracks and vias below them. The copper directly under their metal end caps is the stimulation supply: C4's VCCINT end sits over the +12 V pour, both ends of C42 (VCCO_1V5 and GND) over the -12 V STIM_PRE_NEG pour and a -12 V via, and C59's GND end over the -12 V STIM_NEG_12V pour. Only solder mask, a printed coating about 10-25 um thick, separates them, and the 'PRE-' silkscreen there adds height. If the tolerance stack closes the gap and mating force or head movement wears the mask, +/-12 V reaches a 1.0-1.8 V FPGA supply.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO A V12 top (L1) under Frontend bottom C4 (VCCINT_1V0/GND, LDO frame x 89.70-91.70, y 137.87-139.12), C42 (VCCO_1V5/GND, x 108.34-110.34, y 141.22-142.47) and C59 (VCCAUX_1V8/GND, x 105.85-107.10, y 140.12-142.12). DNP C89 would land over the same +12 V pour.
findings.evidence: Mate transform LDO = (213.5 - x, 239.57 - y), fitted to the J1/J2 connector centres in exports/frontend/pads.csv and exports/ldo_a/pads.csv (same as SYS-08). pcbnew zone fill on a scratch copy (a review working file (not published), under3.py): under the 2.0 x 1.25 mm bodies, L1 copper is STIM_POS_12V 1.33 mm2 (C4), STIM_PRE_NEG 2.42 mm2 plus the via and a track (C42), STIM_NEG_12V 0.79 mm2 plus a GND via (C59). Under the 0.45 mm end bands: C4 VCCINT end over STIM_POS_12V 0.28 mm2; C42 VCCO_1V5 end 0.48 mm2 and GND end 0.56 mm2 over STIM_PRE_NEG; C59 GND end 0.26 mm2 over STIM_NEG_12V. Solder mask is not a rated insulation barrier under pressure and rubbing; a breach puts +12 V on VCCINT or -12 V on VCCO_1V5 and destroys the FPGA, on a stack that moves with the animal.

findings.corrected: On FPGA-LDO A V12, the masked L1 copper under the Frontend's 1.25 ±0.2 mm bottom capacitors is ±12 V stimulation supply, not just tracks and vias. Both C42 terminations (VCCO_1V5 and GND) sit over the -12 V STIM_PRE_NEG pour at every termination width; C59's GND end sits over -12 V STIM_NEG_12V; and C4's VCCINT end sits over the edge of the +12 V STIM_POS_12V copper (0 to 0.59 mm2 for Murata e = 0.2 to 0.7 mm). If SYS-08's worst case (about 0.05 mm at a 1.45 mm part; about 0.2 to 0.25 mm nominal, not 0.1 mm) ever wears through the 10 to 15 um mask, C4 could dump +12 V into VCCINT (1.1 V absolute maximum). The C42 and C59 contacts would only short the -12 V rail, because the 3 A 1.5 V buck holds VCCO. This broadens SYS-08/FE-04, which stay major and do not become a blocker: the ≤0.95 mm part swap or DNP C4 closes it, and FE-04's 'keep C4 and accept the 0.05 mm gap' option should be rejected unless the +12 V copper under C4 is cleared. DNP C89's terminations are not over ±12 V.

C4's VCCINT end covers 0, 0.28 or 0.59 mm² of +12 V copper for Murata end bands of 0.2, 0.45 or 0.7 mm (part thickness 1.25 ±0.2 mm). Only C4 can overstress the FPGA: C14's +12 V charge would flow into VCCINT (DS181 maximum 1.1 V). The 1.5 V buck holds VCCO. Major fits. Nominal gap ≈0.25 mm, not 0.1. C89's ends are not over ±12 V.

findings.title: The 3.3 V contact J2.69 sits next to STIM_START_SHARED on J2.67, so one solder bridge puts 3.3 V on a 1.5 V FPGA output and all eight ASIC inputs.
findings.what: The head's only 3.3 V supply enters on J2.68-70. On the odd row, J2.69 is the neighbour (0.4 mm pitch) of J2.67, STIM_START_SHARED, which runs with no series resistor from FPGA ball B10 in a 1.5 V bank to all eight ASICs. The even-row neighbour J2.66 is GND, but the odd row has no guard. A bridge at either board's DF40 joint (pad gaps about 0.17 mm on this header and 0.20 mm on the Frontend receptacle, with full-size paste per SYS-21) drives 3.3 V into a pin whose absolute maximum is VCCO + 0.55 V, about 2.05 V.

findings.title: Pin map V6 also needs a pull-down on each port's new top-chip SPI_LATCH line (J3/J4 pin 70), which V12 routes as a plain data lane.
findings.what: This board holds every FPGA-to-ASIC control line at a safe level while the FPGA configures, because the Frontend sets PUDC_B high and leaves its pins floating; its own note says SPI_LATCH held low blocks any SPI update. On the received ASIC boards V4 the top chips take their latch and SPI clock from pins 70 and 72 (T_SPI_LATCH, T_SPI_CLK), not from the shared pins 61 and 63. V12 routes pins 70/72 as returned CLK32 and SYNC lanes with no pull, and the V6 change list (12 new routes, 4 clock swaps) adds none, so the top four chips' latch would float during configuration.

merged.title: Pin map V6 makes the far chips' SPI latch an FPGA output with no pull-down, while the near chips' latch keeps R18.
merged.what: On ASIC V4 the near chips latch on pin 61, which R18 holds low on FPGA-LDO A, but the far chips latch on pin 70 (T_SPI_LATCH). The V6 trace only renames pin 70 on each port to an FPGA output (ASIC3_4_TOP_SPI_LATCH, ASIC7_8_TOP_SPI_LATCH) and adds no resistor. V12 has none on that net either; today the net goes to an FPGA input. The far chips' latch therefore floats whenever the FPGA is not driving it: during the roughly 7 s of FPGA configuration, and in any partial-seat window that opens pin 70. In a pin-80-end lift, pin 70 opens at 0.52 mm together with AC_IN.
merged.where: FPGA-LDO A J3.70 (/ASIC7_CLK32MHz_Out to J2.26) and J4.70 (/ASIC3_CLK32MHz_Out to J2.35), even row, x 105.583. On ASIC V4, J3/J4.70 T_SPI_LATCH goes to top U01_BCD1/2 SPI_LATCH. R18 (10k) is only on /SPI_LATCH_SHARED (J2.48, J3.61, J4.61).

findings.title: A J3/J4 joint lifted at the pin-1 end, or rocked toward the probe edge, can open all four grounds while rails, including -10 V, stay connected.
findings.what: All four return contacts (AGND 42/44, GND 46/48) sit in the middle of the even row. DVDD to REF_VCM lie on one side of them and VDD_FE, REF_VDD, VSS10 and VDD_ADC on the other; the odd row has no ground at all. Lifting the pin-1 end of a joint opens the grounds before those four rails. A rock that lifts the even row opens every ground while VDD_CGEN and every control stay connected and driven. Either way the ASICs see powered rails or driven inputs with no return path. This is the J3/J4 form of LDOB-24, and it applies to both options and to the near-to-far joint.

findings.title: The +/-10 V stimulation rails can reach +/-10.3 V, with no ASIC or capacitor rating to show that is safe.
findings.what: R901 and R1001 (100k, 1%) set the stimulation rails ASIC_VDD10 and ASIC_VSS10 to +10.0 V and -10.0 V. The regulator output equals its SET pin current times the SET resistor, and that current varies from 98 to 102 uA over temperature, so the rails can span about 9.70 to 10.30 V in size. The only requirement on file is the ASIC designer's pin sheet, which gives +/-10 V with no maximum or tolerance; the ASIC reference says the chip's '+/-10 V' figure is stimulator output range, not a supply rating. The files cannot settle whether 10.3 V is within the rating of the ASIC and of the four 0201 capacitors on these rails on the ASIC board; a written answer from the ASIC designer would.

findings.what: U8 (LT3042) makes the 0.75 V common-mode reference ASIC_REF_VCM, and below 1 V output the LT3042 needs at least 10 uA of load to stay stable. Nothing on this board or the ASIC board loads the net with a resistor; the ASIC board puts only capacitors and ASIC reference pins on it, and the ASIC's current on this pin is listed as TBD. With no ASIC boards fitted the regulator certainly runs below its minimum load, and with them it may. The inherited LDO Board A had the same gap.

merged.title: U8 holds the 0.75 V REF_VCM inside the LT3042's input-pair transition range, where it cannot sink current and its offset and noise are worse.
merged.what: The LT3042's error amplifier hands over between two input stages between 0.6 V and 1.3 V output. In that range the data sheet allows up to 2 mV of extra offset and 600 nA of extra SET-current change, and doubles the noise. Its output-overshoot current sink is switched off below 1.5 V output, so U8 can only source current. REF_VCM is shared by eight ASICs and has no load resistor (LDOA-14). If the ASIC pins together push current into REF_VCM, the rail drifts up and nothing on the board pulls it back. The worst-case set point is about 0.72-0.78 V (±4 %), and no ASIC tolerance exists to judge it against.
merged.where: FPGA-LDO A V12, U8 (93.2,135.6, bottom), R801 7.5k 1 %, C803 1 uF, output caps C802 10 uF and C57 1 uF, net /ASIC_REF_VCM to J3/J4 pin 40.
merged.evidence: LT3042 Rev A, p.3: change in VOS with VSET from 0 to 1.3 V is 0.3 mV typical, 2 mV maximum; change in ISET is 150 nA typical, 600 nA maximum; ISET is 98-102 uA; RMS noise is 1.6 uVrms for 0 V to 1.3 V output against 0.8 uVrms above. p.4 Note 13: 10 uA minimum load below 1 V. p.14: PNP input pair 0-0.6 V, NPN above 1.3 V. p.19: overshoot-recovery sink disabled below 1.5 V output. Calculation: 0.98 x 0.99 x 0.75 V - 6.5 mV = 0.72 V, and 1.02 x 1.01 x 0.75 V + 6.5 mV = 0.779 V. exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: no resistor on /ASIC_REF_VCM. The ASIC V4 boards add only capacitors C5/C46/C57/C58 on /REF_VCM.
merged.source: ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A (3042fa), p.3, p.4 Note 13, p.14 Output Voltage, p.19 Output Overshoot Recovery, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3042.pdf (saved copy, analog.com unreachable). inputs/asic J3_pinout__Power_Pins.csv (REF_VCM 0.75 V, current TBD).
merged.consequence: The common-mode reference of all eight ASICs is known only to about ±4 %. If the ASIC pins source current, it can sit above its set value with no board-level correction.
merged.suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer for the REF_VCM pin current, its direction, and the allowed tolerance. Size the LDOA-14 load resistor so it draws more than any current the ASICs can push in: 7.5-10 kOhm (75-100 uA) rather than 68 kOhm if the pins can source.

findings.title: One RC starts every ASIC rail with no FPGA control or power-good; the +/-10 V rails need up to about 0.5 s.
findings.what: One resistor-capacitor delay (R1, C3) drives EN_ASIC_RAILS, which enables the LT3582 converter and every regulator; the FPGA cannot switch any rail, and the power-good (PG) outputs that report a rail is in regulation are all left open. Fast start-up is off (PGFB tied to IN), so each rail ramps slowly at a rate set by its SET resistor and capacitor: the 1.5 V LT3042 rails settle about 90 ms after 3.3 V appears and the +/-10 V rails take up to about 0.48 s. The inherited firmware releases CHIP_RESET about 65 ms after FPGA configuration, so it may do so before VDD10/VSS10 are valid. The ASIC reference defines no rail order, so the files cannot say whether this matters; the owner has to decide on firmware delay or hardware control.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO A: R1 (109.4, 140.3), C3 (106.9, 140.3), net /EN_ASIC_RAILS to U1 pin 8 (SHDN), TP4 and the EN pins of U2-U10; PG pin 4 of U2, U6, U8, U9 and U10 unconnected. EN_ASIC_RAILS does not reach J1 or J2. Stimulation power can only be removed by the solder jumpers JP1/JP2.
findings.evidence: exports/ldo_a/netlist.xml: /EN_ASIC_RAILS = C3, R1, TP4, U1.8 and U2-U10 EN; PG pins 'unconnected-'; PGFB = IN on all five LT3042/LT3094. RC timing: R1 10k from VIN_3V3, C3 4.7 uF; Thevenin 10k || 222k (LT3582 SHDN bias) || 125k (four 500k TPS7A20 pull-downs) = 8.9 kOhm, Vinf = 2.93 V, tau = 41.8 ms; 0.9 V reached at 15.3 ms, 1.24 V at 23.0 ms. Soft start, 99% at 4.6 x RSET x CSET: 15k x 1 uF -> 69 ms; 100k x 1 uF -> 460 ms. DC-bias loss on the 25 V 0603 SET capacitors (C903, C1003) probably shortens this to about 0.3-0.45 s (typical X5R behaviour, from memory, not a vendor curve). Schematic note: firmware drives CHIP_RESET high for 2^20 cycles (about 65 ms) at boot. J1 has 13 no-connect pins on both the LDO A and Frontend sides.
findings.source: ADI LT3042 Rev A p.4 (EN/UV threshold) and p.12 (PGFB, fast start-up); ADI LT3094 Rev 0 (start-up time grows with CSET); ADI LT3582 3582512fb (SHDN threshold and current); TI TPS7A20 SBVS338H p.4 and p.7; ASIC_REFERENCE.md open item U02 (no rail sequence).
findings.consequence: The ASICs may leave reset or receive stimulation commands before the +/-10 V rails are valid, and firmware cannot detect it. There is no software way to remove stimulation power in a fault.
findings.suggested_action: At minimum, have firmware wait at least 0.6 s after power-up before releasing CHIP_RESET or enabling stimulation. Better, bring EN_ASIC_RAILS, or a separate enable for U1/U9/U10, to a spare J1 contact driven by the FPGA, which also needs a Frontend change.

findings.title: All 3.3 V input current for the board passes through a single 0.15 mm through via.
findings.what: VIN_3V3 enters on J2.68-70 on the top layer (L1) and reaches the bottom-layer (L6) pour that feeds every regulator through one through via. The expected 167 mA (335 mA in the high case) is well within this via's capacity, and the converter's local input capacitors C1 and C2 sit on L6, so capacity and noise are not the problem. findings.title: Nobody has checked that U10's output capacitors keep the LT3094's 10 uF minimum after DC-bias derating.
findings.what: The LT3094 needs at least 10 uF of ceramic output capacitance to stay stable. U10's output has 32 uF nominal (22 uF 1206 plus 10 uF 0805, both 25 V X5R) at -10 V. Ceramic capacitors lose much of their value under DC voltage (DC-bias derating), heat and tolerance, the small 0805 most of all, and Samsung's product pages give no DC-bias data. The same unchecked question applies to C902 at U9 (LT3042, 4.7 uF minimum, more margin) and to the +/-12 V converter outputs, which sit at 12 V and are likely to lose the largest fraction.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO Option A V12. ASIC_VSS10 (-10 V, R1001 100k): C1002 (CL31A226KAHNNNE) and C1004 (CL21A106KAYNNNE) at U10.10-12. ASIC_VDD10: C902 (CL31A226KAHNNNE) at U9. STIM_POS_12V / STIM_NEG_12V: C14 and C21 (CL21A226MAYNNNE, 22 uF 0805), plus C901/C1001 (10 uF 0805) on STIM_PRE_POS/NEG through the bridged JP1/JP2.
findings.evidence: board.json nets: /ASIC_VSS10 = C1002.1, C1004.1, J3.54, J4.54, U10.10-12; /ASIC_VDD10 = C902.1, J3/J4.36, U9.9/10. parts.csv MPNs as listed. Samsung product pages for CL21A106KAYNNN and CL31A226KAHNNN: 25 V, X5R, +/-10 %, no DC-bias curve. A rough estimate from typical X5R behaviour (from memory, not a datasheet) leaves about 15-18 uF at 10 V, so failure is unlikely but not proven.
findings.source: ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev B, output capacitor section (10 uF ceramic minimum confirmed from ADI's product page, https://www.analog.com/en/products/lt3094.html); LT3042 Rev B (4.7 uF minimum). The data sheet PDFs could not be opened, so the ESR limit and page numbers were not checked against the datasheet.
findings.consequence: If the effective capacitance at -10 V and temperature falls below 10 uF, the -10 V ASIC rail can ring or oscillate.
findings.suggested_action: Read Samsung's DC-bias curves for these parts at 10 V and 12 V (or measure them); if the -10 V total falls below about 13 uF at 25 C, make C1004 a second 22 uF 1206.

findings.title: U1 has no fixed frequency, so its ripple can alias into the recording band as a tone that moves with load.
findings.what: U1 (LT3582-12) has no fixed-frequency or sync mode: its frequency sits near 48-52 kHz at light load and rises with load. Each ASIC channel is sampled at 31.25 kS/s, so ripple that reaches a sampled node shows up 'aliased' (folded) at |f - n x 31.25 kHz|, somewhere between 0 and 15.6 kHz, and that tone moves when the ±12 V load changes. Folding itself is not new: the replaced TPS65130 (1.25-1.50 MHz) and the Frontend's MPM3833C that makes VIN_3V3 (about 1.15 MHz) also alias into the band; what U1 adds is a load-dependent tone. The ripple level that reaches the ASIC is not known and has not been worked out, so only a bring-up measurement can settle whether it matters.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO Option A, U1 LT3582EUD-12 (bottom, pin 12 SW_P, pins 3/4 SW_N, pin 5 VIN on VIN_3V3). U1 feeds only U9 LT3042 (ASIC_VDD10, via STIM_POS_12V, JP1, STIM_PRE_POS) and U10 LT3094 (ASIC_VSS10, via STIM_NEG_12V, JP2, STIM_PRE_NEG). The other seven LDOs (U2-U8) see U1 only through its input-current pulses on VIN_3V3 and through GND/AGND (NT1). Bench option: TP8/TP9, TP6 AGND.

Scaling the boost to VIN 3.3 V by the DCM energy ratio (12.5/7.5 vs 12.5/9.2, factor 1.227) gives about 183/346/785 kHz; the inverter does not change with VIN. Loads: LT3042 quiescent about 2 mA, LT3094 about 2.35 mA; the ASIC designer's budget (J3_pinout__Power_Budget.csv) gives 2 mA each on VDD10/VSS10 per board, about 10 mA per output for four boards; 8 ASICs x 128 x 22.5 uA = 23 mA with all stimulators on. TPS65130 1.25-1.50 MHz spans 40-48 x 31.25 kHz; MPM3833C 1.15 MHz folds to about 6.25 kHz. LT3042/LT3094 PSRR at 1 MHz 79/74 dB (front pages). Schematic V30A LT3582 note lists 'ripple after layout' as unverified; parts review V21 still gives the TPS65130 fixed-frequency rationale.
findings.source: ADI LT3582/LT3582-5/LT3582-12 data sheet 3582512fb, Rev B: p.6 G01, p.7 G10-G14, p.10 Operation, p.19, p.22 Figure 13, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf; TI TPS65130 SLVS493E p.6 (fS); MPS MPM3833C product page (forced CCM frequency); inputs/asic/ASIC_Reference/ASIC_REFERENCE.md B6 (0.3-10 kHz), B12 (31.25 kS/s), B16 (22.5 uA), B18 (stimulation under 200 Hz), 6.5 uVrms integrated noise.
findings.consequence: If enough ripple survives the ASIC's supply rejection (no ASIC specification gives it), recordings could show narrow tones in the 0.3-10 kHz band whose frequency depends on the unit and the static stimulator load. A bad result costs a jumper cut and a bench supply, not a board spin.
findings.suggested_action: At bring-up, record ASIC shorted-input spectra with U1 running and with JP1/JP2 cut and bench ±12 V on TP8/TP9, at idle and with dummy loads, and look for tones at |f_sw - n x 31.25 kHz| against the 6.5 uVrms noise figure.

findings.title: Nothing discharges the ±10 V ASIC rails, so they can stay charged for seconds after the 1.5 V rails fall.
findings.what: When VIN_3V3 goes away, the 1.5 V regulators lose their input and their outputs fall with it. ASIC_VDD10 and ASIC_VSS10 have no bleed resistor and drain only through the ASIC and regulator leakage, so with little ASIC current they stay near ±10 V for hundreds of milliseconds to seconds. The built-in discharge features do not help: the TPS7A2015 pulldown acts only while EN is low and input is still present, and the LT3582 discharge acts only on its own ±12 V outputs, not on the LT3042/LT3094 outputs. No ASIC power-down requirement exists, so the files cannot say whether the ASIC tolerates live stimulator rails over an unpowered core; only the ASIC designer can.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO Option A: ASIC_VDD10 (U9 LT3042 OUT, C902 22 uF, J3/J4 pin 36) and ASIC_VSS10 (U10 LT3094 OUT, C1002 22 uF + C1004 10 uF, J3/J4 pin 54). 1.5 V rails from U3/U4/U5/U7 TPS7A2015PDQNR and U2/U6/U8 LT3042, all fed from VIN_3V3. EN_ASIC_RAILS from R1 10k / C3 4.7 uF.

TPS7A20 SBVS338H: 150 ohm output pulldown only when VEN < VEN(LOW) = 0.3 V (spec at VIN 3.1 V). LT3582 3582512fb: VIN minimum 2.4-2.55 V (p.2); output discharge permanently enabled on the -12 version and acts on SHDN falling (p.10, p.16). Prior shutdown model (shutdown2_out.txt) at 0 mA ASIC load: VDD10 still 10.00 V at 0.8 s (idealised, no leakage), VSS10 to about -9.45 / -8.19 V through the LT3094 OUT-to-IN path. ASIC_REFERENCE.md sections 4, 7 and 10 give no rail sequence or window.
findings.source: TI TPS7A20 data sheet SBVS338H, p.3 EN pin and p.7 electrical characteristics, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps7a20.pdf; ADI LT3582 data sheet 3582512fb Rev B, p.2, p.10, p.16, https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3582512fb.pdf. findings.consequence: If the ASIC needs its ±10 V rails to fall before or with its 1.5 V rails, every unplug or host shutdown leaves the stimulator supply live over an unpowered core, with undefined stimulator state. If it does not, there is no effect.
findings.suggested_action: Ask the ASIC designer whether VDD10/VSS10 may stay live while the 1.5 V rails are off; if not, add a bleed resistor from each ±10 V rail to AGND (for example 10-22 kOhm, about 5-10 mW).

findings.title: The LT3582 layout leaves out the ground-plane cuts and the extra exposed-pad vias of data sheet Figure 12, so its switching currents spread through the L3/L4 GND planes.
findings.what: The LT3582 data sheet asks for a ground plane under the switcher and for the ground-plane cuts of its Figure 12. These cuts put the inverter's output capacitor and the boost's CAPP/output capacitors on separate cut-off islands joined under the chip, so the converter's current steps recombine under U1 instead of spreading through the plane. The figure also draws about five vias in the exposed pad. On V12 every converter part drops straight into the solid L3/L4 GND planes through its own via, the parts spread over about 18 mm, U1's exposed pad has two vias, and the boost's switching loop closes through about 10 mm of plane. These planes are also the return for the J1/J2 digital lanes, the L5 lane reference and the ground of U3 (VDD_ADC). The 'plane under the switcher' part is met (L5 under the switch-node copper is clear). LDOA-06 covers only the input-capacitor loop, and the missing cuts are on no list.

findings.title: U9, U10 and the TPS7A20 regulators reach ground only through long, shared thin traces; U9's pad has no via.
findings.what: L6 has no ground pour, so U9 (LT3042, VDD10), U10 (LT3094, VSS10) and the TPS7A20 regulators U3/U4/U5 reach their ground plane through daisy-chained 0.10-0.30 mm traces, and U9's exposed pad (the metal pad under the package) has no via. A low-noise regulator sets its output from the voltage on its SET resistor, so any voltage drop between the SET resistor's ground and the plane adds straight onto the output. For U9 that drop path also carries C901's input ripple return and U5's capacitor currents. For U10 the SET resistor's ground leg carries the output capacitors' transient current and U10's own ground current, but not the DC load return of this negative regulator.

merged.title: U10's whole ground network, SET reference included, reaches AGND through one microvia that also carries C1001's converter ripple, so roughly 0.04-0.16 mV rms of switching ripple lands on VSS10.
merged.area: LDO layout vs ADI SET/COUT/CIN ground rules
merged.what: ADI's layout rules (LT3094 p.15/p.18, LT3042 p.13/p.15) are: the SET capacitor's ground ties directly to the output capacitor's ground, the input and output capacitor grounds sit close together, and the SET resistor's ground is Kelvin-connected to the load. The LT3042 copy calls this 'very important for stability'. On U10, every ground connection (GND pin, ILIM, C1002, C1004, CSET C1003, RSET R1001 and input capacitor C1001) is one daisy chain of 0.15-0.30 mm L6 traces. That chain reaches the L2 AGND plane only through a single 0.10 mm microvia at C1001. The share of the LT3582 inverter ripple carried by C1001 goes down that via, so the SET reference rides on the via's voltage drop and U10 copies it straight to VSS10, bypassing its PSRR. findings.title: The order sets no bottom stencil thickness; above 0.10 mm the X2SON pin apertures release paste poorly.
findings.what: Solder paste leaves a stencil hole cleanly only if the hole's open area is large compared with its wall area; this 'area ratio' is usually kept at 0.66 or more (IPC-7525 guideline). The X2SON pin apertures of the four TPS7A2015 regulators copy TI's own example stencil, which TI bases on a 0.075-0.1 mm stencil, giving 0.61 at 0.10 mm, 0.51 at 0.12 mm and 0.41 at 0.15 mm. The assembly remark does not name a stencil thickness, and JLC publishes no default for its assembly service; because the bottom side also carries the 0.4 mm pitch J4, 0.10-0.12 mm is the likely choice and 0.15 mm unlikely. Separately, the exposed-pad (EP, the centre thermal pad) paste is a 45-degree rounded square with 24 % more paste than TI's round aperture.
findings.evidence: B_Paste.gbp in FPGA_LDO_A_V12_gerbers.zip and footprint Texas_X2SON-4_1x1mm_P0.65mm.kicad_mod: pin aperture 0.40 x 0.21 mm with 0.18 mm chamfer, area 0.0678 mm2, perimeter 1.115 mm. Area ratio A/(P x t) = 0.61 / 0.51 / 0.41 at t = 0.10 / 0.12 / 0.15 mm. J4 (0.4 mm DF40, bottom): 0.80 / 0.67 / 0.54 at the same thicknesses; DFN and QFN pins about 0.83-0.84 at 0.12 mm. findings.title: Three polarized bottom parts (U1, D12, J4) are at 0 or 180 degrees in the CPL, and a half-turn on U1 or D12 shorts the 3.3 V input or drives the -12 V rail positive.
findings.what: The CPL gives JLC KiCad's raw angles for all 68 bottom parts. If the bottom angle is taken as 180 minus the KiCad angle, as common JLC tools write it (FE-12), the parts at 0 or 180 degrees turn by half a turn: U1, D12 and J4. U1 turned puts its GND pin 13 on the VIN_3V3 pad and its VIN pin on GND, a dead short of the stack's 3.3 V. D12 reversed lets the inverter switch drive STIM_NEG_12V and the LT3094 input to about +2.9 V, past its +0.3 V limit, and leaves the inductor current no path. Under the opposite convention (angle negated) D11 and U2-U10 at +/-90 degrees turn instead, so the preview check must cover all 13 polarized bottom parts.

To check them at first power-up, someone has to hold a probe on the regulators' output-capacitor pads on the bottom side; seven of these are small 0402/0603 parts. findings.title: The LT3094 rejects little of the inverter's fast edges near 10 MHz, so VSS10 edge noise is unbounded on paper.
findings.what: The LT3582 converter makes the +/-12 V supplies by switching, which leaves ripple at its switching frequency plus fast nanosecond edges, mostly on the -12 V side. The LT3094 that makes VSS10 has a PSRR (power-supply rejection ratio: how much input noise it keeps off its output) of about 80 dB near 1 MHz but only about 25-35 dB at 10 MHz, and its data sheet gives nothing higher. The LT3042 that makes VDD10 still gives about 57-80 dB at 10 MHz, so VDD10 is less exposed. How much edge noise reaches VSS10 depends on layout and output capacitors and must be measured.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO A V12: D12 / C21 / JP2 / C1001 -> U10 (LT3094, VSS10, output caps C1002, C1004); D11 / C15 / C14 / JP1 / C901 -> U9 (LT3042, VDD10, output cap C902); both rails reach the ASIC boards through J4.
findings.evidence: LT3094 Rev 0 p.11 G45 and p.12 G46 at IL = -1 mA: about 85 dB near 100 kHz, 78-80 dB at 1 MHz, peak near 2 MHz, about 25-35 dB at 10 MHz. LT3042 Rev A p.10 G43 at 1 mA: about 84 dB at 1 MHz, 76-80 dB at 10 MHz; p.9 G41/G42: about 57-65 dB at 10 MHz at 50-200 mA. The review's ripple model (outside.py, not re-run by the checker): VOUTN 1.6 / 4.3 / 6.4 mV rms and VOUTP 0.5-0.8 mV rms at 2 / 10 / 25 mA, edge spikes on VOUTN about 0.1 V p-p, sensitive to assumed capacitor ESL. nets.csv gives the regulator and output-capacitor nets.
findings.source: ADI LT3094 data sheet Rev 0, p.11-12 (G45-G47), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/lt3094.pdf; ADI LT3042 data sheet Rev A, p.9-10 (G41-G43), https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/3042fb.pdf; LT3582 data sheet p.22 (output ripple reference).
findings.consequence: Probably harmless for stimulation, but VSS10 also feeds the ASIC and shares its AGND, so unmeasured high-frequency content is a possible path for noise into recordings.
findings.suggested_action: Add VSS10 and VDD10 at the J4 pins to the bring-up ripple measurement, using a 20 MHz-bandwidth probe with a short ground spring.

findings.title: C1001 and C901 probably fall below the LT3094's 10 uF and the LT3042's 4.7 uF minimum input capacitance at 12 V bias; only the output side was being tracked.
findings.what: ADI also gives input minimums: the LT3094 is stable with at least 10 uF on IN (p.20) and the LT3042 with at least 4.7 uF (Rev A p.16). The only local input capacitors of U10 and U9 are 10 uF 25 V 0805 X5R parts (C1001, C901) biased at 12 V. Parts like these usually keep well under half their value at that voltage; this is an estimate, because Samsung's DC-bias data could not be read. The converter's 22 uF capacitors C21 and C14 are on the same nets, through JP2/JP1 and some trace. The oscillation risk looks low: about 12 nH of feed with about 4 uF local gives a resonance near 0.7 MHz with Q around 1.

findings.title: Many L1 lanes run directly over other nets' L2 lanes, and L5 lanes sit closer to L6 rail pours than to L4 GND.
findings.what: L1-L2 and L5-L6 are only 0.071 mm apart, while L4-L5 is 0.201 mm. Where one trace runs directly over another net's trace on the next layer ('broadside' coupling), the two couple strongly, and an L5 trace over an L6 rail pour returns its current partly through that rail rather than through GND. L2, named the AGND plane, carries 466 mm of signal tracks, which is why L1 lanes sit over L2 lanes. The amounts are modest at these lengths, but no signal-integrity check has been made.

findings.title: The board's minimum solder-mask web is 0, so DRC would not catch a thin mask sliver added by a later edit.
findings.what: Solder mask is the coating between pads; the thin strip of mask left between two pad openings is called the mask web or dam. KiCad only checks these strips against the board's minimum web setting, and on this board that setting is 0, so DRC reports only openings that actually touch. The custom rule file covers via rings, hole clearance, edge clearance and silkscreen, not mask webs. Today the smallest real web is about 0.17 mm, above JLC's 0.10 mm green limit, so nothing is wrong now.
findings.where: FPGA-LDO A V12: FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_pcb setup block (no solder_mask_min_width, so it defaults to 0; pad_to_mask_clearance 0); FPGA_LDO_A_Layout_V12.kicad_dru. Smallest webs at J1 DF40 pads and at the X2SON U3/U4/U5/U7 pin openings next to the exposed-pad opening.
findings.evidence: Board file: pcbnew reports m_SolderMaskMinWidth 0.0. Scratch DRC (KiCad 10.0.6): web 0.10 mm or 0.13 mm gives no new violations; 0.18 mm gives 199 solder_mask_bridge errors (DF40 pads), which shows the check works once set. Mask-web scan: smallest 0.170 mm (J1 DF40 pads; X2SON pin openings to EP opening, mask margin -0.05 mm). The V12 record's 0.12 mm figure is the X2SON copper pad-to-pad gap, not the mask web. The .kicad_pro sets lib_footprint_mismatch, lib_footprint_issues, track_not_centered_on_via, missing_courtyard, footprint_filters_mismatch and footprint_type_mismatch to ignore; turned to warnings they give 53 lib_footprint_mismatch + 12 track_not_centered_on_via and nothing else (library comparison: pad positions and sizes equal the library for every footprint type).
findings.source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities, solder mask bridge 0.10 mm green / 0.13 mm black and white (1 oz), https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities; KiCad DRC solder_mask_bridge behaviour.

findings.title: The Frontend pin constraints set no DRIVE or SLEW on the FPGA outputs to the ASICs, so their edge rate is never chosen.
findings.what: Every ASIC-facing ball is set only to LVCMOS15, so Vivado uses its defaults of 12 mA drive and SLOW slew. SLOW is the right choice for these 32-60 kHz strobes and slow SPI lines. Writing DRIVE 4 or 8 and SLEW SLOW explicitly would lower their dI/dt and the STIM_CLK-to-STIM_START/EN crosstalk, and would protect them against a later global change. This does not help the CLK32 clocks, whose aggressors are ASIC outputs.
findings.where: W2/inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: STIM_START/EN/CLK/CHB_SHARED (B10, J6, B11, V9), BOARD1/3_CLK (G16, V17), BOARD1/3_SPI_CLK (D10, V8), SPI_LATCH_SHARED (D11), CHIP_RESET_SHARED (C9), STIM_CHIP1-4_SPI_DL/DR and the V4 top-chip SPI outputs.
findings.evidence: grep of the XDC: 116 constraints, no DRIVE, SLEW or PULL property. Crosstalk from STIM_CLK onto STIM_START at the ASIC is 91 mV at 1 ns and 124 mV at 0.5 ns (25 ohm), and 27-28 mV at 2 ns (run2ns.json).
findings.source: AMD UG471 7 Series FPGAs SelectIO Resources User Guide v1.10 (8 May 2018), p.48 (SLEW default SLOW; DRIVE default 12; Table 1-8: LVCMOS15 HR 4, 8, 12 or 16 mA) and p.56 (Table 1-14); https://docs.amd.com/v/u/en-US/ug471_7Series_SelectIO (returned HTTP 404 today; read from a review working file (not published)).
findings.consequence: None today, because SLOW is the default. The FPGA-side edge rate is unrecorded, so the 0.5 ns cases cannot be ruled out on paper.
findings.suggested_action: Add DRIVE 8 (or 4) and SLEW SLOW to the ASIC-facing output constraints, and check the edge rate in Vivado's IBIS export.

findings.title: Option A has four SPI data pairs for eight ASICs, so each near/far ASIC pair gets identical configuration.
findings.closed_by: Closed in V3: Closed by the ASIC boards V4 and the owner's 11 Nov evening decision. Each far (top) chip now has its own SPI_DINR/DINL: pins 16/18 for U01_BCD2 and 66/68 for U01_BCD1. The far board also has its own latch on pin 70 and clock on pin 72, which the near board only passes through. FPGA-LDO A V12 and the Frontend already carry these 12 lanes as routed copper to 12 separate U1 balls (T15, R13, M2, M4, N3, N4; C18, D18, T7, R5, P4, P3). So all 16 SPI data inputs in a stack reach 16 different FPGA balls, and near/far chips cannot get identical configuration. The remaining work belongs to A-P. The V6 pin file and gateware must drive these balls as LVCMOS15 outputs; until then, the far chips' SPI inputs float on FPGA inputs. One minor item goes on the V6 change list: J3.70/J4.70 have no 10k pull-down like R18 on SPI_LATCH_SHARED. While the FPGA configures, the far chips are guarded only by the CHIP_RESET pull-up R19, and its reset polarity comes from firmware and is unverified.
